Caro-Kann Defense.name: Caro-Kann Defense, General
Caro-Kann Defense.context: Caro-Kann Defense: A solid opening for Black after 1.e4 c6. Black intends to challenge White's center with a timely ...d5, keeping a resilient structural layout.

Caro-Kann Defense.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Two Knights Variation
Caro-Kann Defense.context: Two Knights Variation: White develops both knights early to pressure d5, bypassing traditional main lines and opting for open, rapid piece-play.

Caro-Kann Defense.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Advance Variation
Caro-Kann Defense.context: Advance Variation: White grabs space by pushing e5. Black usually counters by activating the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain with ...Bf5.

Caro-Kann Defense.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Exchange Variation
Caro-Kann Defense.pgn: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 cxd5
Caro-Kann Defense.context: Exchange Variation: Liquidating the central tension early leads to a symmetrical pawn skeleton where piece positioning and minor imbalances dictate the middlegame.

Caro-Kann Defense.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Panov-Botvinnik Attack
Caro-Kann Defense.pgn: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 cxd5 4. c4
Caro-Kann Defense.context: Panov-Botvinnik Attack: White introduces dynamic asymmetry by striking at d5 with c4, often leading to an Isolated Queen's Pawn (IQP) setup with sharp attacking chances.

Caro-Kann Defense.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Classical Variation
Caro-Kann Defense.pgn: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Bf5
Caro-Kann Defense.context: Classical Variation: The traditional absolute main line where Black develops the light-squared bishop actively to f5 before securing the e6-d5 pawn skeleton.

Scandinavian Defense.name: Scandinavian Defense, General
Scandinavian Defense.context: Scandinavian Defense: An immediate counter-strike in the center. Black forces open lines and quick development right from the very first move.

Scandinavian Defense.name: Scandinavian Defense: Main Line (3...Qa5)
Scandinavian Defense.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qa5
Scandinavian Defense.context: Main Line Qa5: Black accepts an early queen foray, using the a5 square as a safe anchor while executing a solid, light-squared pawn layout.

Scandinavian Defense.name: Scandinavian Defense: Gubinsky-Melts Variation (3...Qd6)
Scandinavian Defense.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qd6
Scandinavian Defense.context: Gubinsky-Melts Variation: An active queen retreat to d6 that keeps pressure on White's d-pawn while preparing queenside castling or rapid central operations.

Scandinavian Defense.name: Scandinavian Defense: Pytel-Wittmann Variation (3...Qd8)
Scandinavian Defense.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qd8
Scandinavian Defense.context: Pytel-Wittmann Variation: A total retreat of the queen to its starting square, prioritizing absolute safety and treating the opening like an asymmetrical counter-punch.

Scandinavian Defense.name: Scandinavian Defense: Modern Variation
Scandinavian Defense.context: Modern Variation: Black avoids bringing the queen out too early, opting instead to recapture the d5 pawn with a knight, maintaining dynamic flexibility.

Scandinavian Defense.name: Scandinavian Defense: Richter Gambit
Scandinavian Defense.pgn: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. d4 Bg4
Scandinavian Defense.context: Richter Gambit: An aggressive system where Black plays an early ...Bg4 pinning White's f3 defenses to disrupt developmental cohesion.

Modern Defense.name: Modern Defense, General
Modern Defense.context: Modern Defense: A hypermodern response allowing White a full center while Black plans a swift flank attack using the g7-fianchetto.

Modern Defense.name: Modern Defense: King's Pawn Fianchetto
Modern Defense.context: King's Pawn Fianchetto: The cornerstone setup of the Modern Defense, maximizing the dark-squared bishop's influence down the long diagonal.

Modern Defense.name: Modern Defense: Pseudo-Austrian Attack
Modern Defense.context: Pseudo-Austrian Attack: White advances three central pawns to smother Black's position, creating extreme space advantages balanced by structural targets for Black.

Modern Defense.name: Modern Defense: 150 Attack (Be3/Qd2 setup)
Modern Defense.pgn: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Bg7 3. Nc3 d6 4. Be3 Nf6 5. Qd2
Modern Defense.context: 150 Attack: White establishes a cohesive battery with Be3 and Qd2, plotting a direct kingside assault via an h4-h5 storm or trade of dark bishops.

Dutch Defense.name: Dutch Defense
Dutch Defense.context: Dutch Defense: Black stakes a claim on e4 with the f-pawn and builds either the Classical set-up (…e6, …Be7, …d6) or the Stonewall (…e6, …d5, …c6, …Bd6), aiming for a kingside initiative.

Vienna Opening.name: Vienna Opening, General
Vienna Opening.context: Vienna Opening: White develops the queenside knight to c3, keeping the f-pawn unblocked and retaining the option of an aggressive f4 thrust.

Vienna Opening.name: Vienna Gambit
Vienna Opening.context: Vienna Gambit: An aggressive flank gambit akin to the King's Gambit but with a protected c3 knight, generating severe attacking pressure on the f-file.

Scotch Opening.name: Scotch Opening: General / Gambit Lines
Scotch Opening.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Bc4
Scotch Opening.context: Scotch Gambit: White offers up the d4 pawn in exchange for sweeping piece activity, lightning-fast development, and early kingside mating patterns.

Scotch Opening.name: Scotch Opening: Goering Gambit
Scotch Opening.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. c3
Scotch Opening.context: Goering Gambit: A hyper-aggressive sacrifice where White gives up one or two pawns on c3 and b2 to gain wide open diagonals for the bishop pair.

Scotch Opening.name: Scotch Opening: Main Line
Scotch Opening.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4
Scotch Opening.context: Scotch Main Line: White recaptures on d4 immediately, staking a claim in the center and avoiding lengthy Ruy Lopez or Italian game theories.

Scotch Opening.name: Scotch Opening: Four Knights Variation
Scotch Opening.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3
Scotch Opening.context: Scotch Four Knights: A highly symmetrical and solid variation that focuses heavily on positional precision and structural imbalances.

Queen's Gambit.name: Queen's Gambit: Marshall Defense
Queen's Gambit.context: Marshall Defense: Black defends d5 with a knight. While playable, it often allows White to exchange on d5 and build a dominant pawn center.

Queen's Gambit.name: Queen's Gambit: Chigorin Defense
Queen's Gambit.context: Chigorin Defense: An energetic, tactical counter-defense where Black blocks the c-pawn with ...Nc6, seeking immediate piece pressure against White's center.

Queen's Gambit.name: Queen's Gambit: Albin Counter-Gambit
Queen's Gambit.context: Albin Counter-Gambit: Black strikes back immediately with 2...e5, muddying tactical waters and introducing complex trap-laden variations.

Queen's Gambit.name: Queen's Gambit: Slav Defense
Queen's Gambit.context: Slav Defense: A rock-solid response. Black supports d5 with ...c6, ensuring a sturdy pawn shell while leaving the light-squared bishop unobstructed.

Queen's Gambit.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted
Queen's Gambit.context: Queen's Gambit Accepted: Black surrenders the central d5 strongpoint temporarily, focusing on quick piece play and dynamic counterstrikes on the flank.

Queen's Gambit.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Orthodox Main Line
Queen's Gambit.pgn: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5
Queen's Gambit.context: Orthodox Main Line: The classic pinnacle of Queen's Gambit theory. White creates a strong pin on f6 while Black prepares a safe, resilient kingside fortress.
